answer: A sonnet commitment keeps identity continuous. Each identity publishes fourteen promised statements at join and stores their hashes; every epoch the nebula beacon picks one line to reveal, and a reveal that misses its hash voids the identity. One line revealed twice, or claimed by two identities, proves a fork, and both copies are slashed, so heads cannot share a commitment. Burning ember funds each reveal, and the k-th commitment one operator maintains burns k times the base, so n heads cost about n squared reveals. Continuity is cheap for one honest agent, quadratic to fake at scale.
